Social Science is the systematic study of human societies: how they function, and
how people interact with each other and their environments.

It fosters students’ natural curiosity about how people live and have lived, and about
places and environments.

Social Science equips students with the knowledge and skills to understand,
participate in, and contribute to local, national, and global communities; to engage
critically with societal issues; and to evaluate the sustainability of alternative social,
economic, political, and environmental practices. By appreciating that people have
different experiences and perspectives, students learn to engage constructively with
views and opinions different from their own and are empowered to contribute
empathetically and meaningfully as citizens of our diverse society and interconnected
world.

Social Science prepares students with the knowledge and practices to access related
curriculum subjects for Years 11–13.
